condition: Amsterdam residents face recurring explosions and violent incidents that may reduce actual and perceived public safety (simulation seed, synthetic evidence).
affected: Residents, businesses and visitors in the area, and emergency responders who attend incidents, as groups; the size of each group is not known in this seed.

place.coarse_area: Amsterdam, districts not named in this seed

since.started: Synthetic series starts in the first quarter of the invented data

observed_facts.statement: The invented incident-pattern table shows 39 explosive-device incidents over four quarters (synthetic).
In the invented survey summary, 34 percent of 1200 respondents feel unsafe after dark (synthetic).
The invented response-time table shows the median arrival time for explosive-device incidents rising from 9 to 11 minutes (synthetic).

uncertain_claims.statement: Incident numbers may be rising overall (synthetic items disagree).
uncertain_claims.why_uncertain: The incident-pattern table and the contradicting item show different trends.
uncertain_claims.what_would_settle_it: A third synthetic series using one counting method for both.

uncertain_claims.statement: Perceived safety may follow actual incident counts (hypothesis).
uncertain_claims.why_uncertain: The survey and the counts cover different periods in this synthetic data.
uncertain_claims.what_would_settle_it: Survey and counts for the same quarters.

sources.establishes: Invented quarterly incident counts by category.
sources.authenticity_note: Synthetic: invented for simulation, not real data.

sources.establishes: Invented share of respondents who feel unsafe after dark.
sources.authenticity_note: Synthetic: invented for simulation, not real data.

sources.establishes: Invented median response times by category.
sources.authenticity_note: Synthetic: invented for simulation, not real data.

sources.establishes: An invented series that disagrees with the incident-pattern table.
sources.authenticity_note: Synthetic: invented for simulation, not real data.

evidence_refs.description: Invented quarterly counts of incidents by category (synthetic).
evidence_refs.supports: That incident categories and counts can be described.

evidence_refs.description: Invented survey summary on feeling unsafe after dark (synthetic).
evidence_refs.supports: That perceived safety can be measured as a share.

evidence_refs.description: Invented series that disagrees with the table (synthetic).
evidence_refs.supports: That the trend is contested and needs one counting method.

causal_hypothesis.statement: Weak lighting, long waiting times and few safe crossings may add to how unsafe people feel, whatever the incident counts are (hypothesis, untested).

scope: Structural public safety measures such as lighting, crossings and response waiting times, in the synthetic Amsterdam setting; no individual cases.
desired_outcome: Fewer residents report feeling unsafe after dark, measured by the same survey before and after a pilot of a structural measure.

final_acceptance_criteria.statement: The share of respondents who feel unsafe after dark falls by at least five points in the pilot area.
final_acceptance_criteria.how_observed: The same survey, run before and after the pilot, compared by method and sample.

final_acceptance_criteria.statement: The report states what the survey does not show.
final_acceptance_criteria.how_observed: A second contributor checks the report for a limits section.

assumptions.statement: The invented tables use one counting method.
assumptions.how_to_check: Compare the notes of the incident-pattern table and the contradicting item.

assumptions.statement: Perceived safety responds to lighting and crossings.
assumptions.how_to_check: Pilot a measure and run the survey before and after.

assumptions.statement: No legal judgement is made here; the Amsterdam legal layers are unreviewed stubs and are not judged.
Policing and justice powers sit with other bodies than this problem can change.
assumptions.how_to_check: Read the role map from the competence stage.

out_of_scope: Naming or investigating any person or group.
Any claim about a real incident or a real office's performance.

options: Improve street lighting in a bounded pilot area.
Publish response waiting times in a plain table.

existing_efforts: Unknown in this seed; the invented budget table lists lighting, mediation and outreach lines as examples only.

stage_plan.name: understand_incidents
stage_plan.label: Understand the incidents
stage_plan.goal: Describe the incident categories and how they changed over the invented series, with the uncertainty stated.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A public summary lists each incident category and its trend with the evidence behind it.
acceptance_criteria.measure: Summary checked against the incident-pattern table and the contradicting item.

stage_plan.name: map_competences
stage_plan.label: Map who is responsible for what
stage_plan.goal: List which public bodies hold which duties for prevention, response and justice, as roles, with every legal point marked not judged.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A role map names the duty each body holds, with a source or a not-judged mark.
acceptance_criteria.measure: Map reviewed against the unreviewed competence skeleton.

stage_plan.name: design_prevention
stage_plan.label: Design a prevention option
stage_plan.goal: Choose one structural prevention option (lighting, crossings, waiting times) that fits the findings and the competences.

acceptance_criteria.statement: One option is chosen with its cost band, owner role and civil-liberty check.
acceptance_criteria.measure: Decision record lists the option and the checks.

stage_plan.name: implement_pilot
stage_plan.label: Run a small pilot
stage_plan.goal: Run the chosen option in a bounded area for a fixed period and record what was done.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The pilot ran for the planned period in the planned area.
acceptance_criteria.measure: Implementer log and a verification note.

stage_plan.name: measure_outcome
stage_plan.label: Measure the outcome
stage_plan.goal: Measure the agreed indicator before and after the pilot and report the result with its limits.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The indicator is measured before and after with the same method.
acceptance_criteria.measure: Survey share who feel unsafe after dark, compared before and after.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The report states what the measurement does not show.
acceptance_criteria.measure: Report section reviewed by a second contributor.

constraints.statement: Legal layers are unreviewed stubs; nothing is judged lawful or unlawful.
Policing and justice competences lie with other bodies.
